title: Architecture Decision: PostgreSQL as Primary Relational Store
author: Elena Vance (Principal Architect), Marcus Brody (Lead DB Admin)
event: Architecture proposal for PostgreSQL in Core Platform
context: ACID compliance, robust JSONB support, extensive ecosystem, and strong team familiarity.
decision: Adopt PostgreSQL 15 as the canonical relational data store for user, billing, and transactional data.
action: Adopted PostgreSQL for Core Platform
outcome: Zero data corruption incidents. Required connection pooling (PgBouncer) once service count exceeded 12.
lesson: PostgreSQL connection limits are easily hit under microservice architectures without centralized pooling.
summary: Decision to adopt PostgreSQL. Outcome: Zero data corruption incidents. Required connection pooling (PgBouncer) once service count exceeded 12.. Lesson: PostgreSQL connection limits are easily hit under microservice architectures without centralized pooling.

title: Architecture Decision: Redis for Recommendation Service Caching
author: Dave Chen (Senior Engineer), Priya Sharma (Backend Lead)
event: Architecture proposal for Redis in Recommendation Service
context: Sub-millisecond read latency needed to satisfy <50ms p99 SLA for the recommendation widget.
decision: Introduce a shared Redis cluster as a caching layer in front of PostgreSQL for recommendation score lookups.
action: Adopted Redis for Recommendation Service
outcome: Initially succeeded, but later suffered cache stampedes and serialization overhead under bursty workload.
lesson: Global shared cache without jittered TTLs and request coalescing creates severe thundering herd vulnerabilities under write-heavy bursts.
summary: Decision to adopt Redis. Outcome: Initially succeeded, but later suffered cache stampedes and serialization overhead under bursty workload.. Lesson: Global shared cache without jittered TTLs and request coalescing creates severe thundering herd vulnerabilities under write-heavy bursts.

title: Architecture Decision: Migration from Firebase Auth to Custom JWT & OAuth2
author: Sarah Jenkins (Security Lead), Dave Chen (Senior Engineer)
event: Architecture proposal for JWT & OAuth2 (Hydra/Custom) in Auth Service
context: Enterprise customers required custom SAML/SSO integration, strict VPC data residency, and Firebase rate limits were throttling multi-tenant bursts.
decision: Migrate away from Firebase Authentication in favor of self-hosted OAuth2 + RS256 signed JWT tokens.
action: Adopted JWT & OAuth2 (Hydra/Custom) for Auth Service
outcome: Significantly increased flexibility and reduced monthly SaaS bills by $4,200, but required dedicated maintenance for key rotation.
lesson: Custom auth unlocks enterprise compliance but demands strict automated token rotation and session revocation infrastructure.
summary: Decision to adopt JWT & OAuth2 (Hydra/Custom). Outcome: Significantly increased flexibility and reduced monthly SaaS bills by $4,200, but required dedicated maintenance for key rotation.. Lesson: Custom auth unlocks enterprise compliance but demands strict automated token rotation and session revocation infrastructure.

title: Architecture Decision: Event-Driven Microservices with Apache Kafka
author: Elena Vance (Principal Architect), Alex Rivera (Infra Lead)
event: Architecture proposal for Apache Kafka in Event Bus
context: Decouple synchronous HTTP request chains across billing, notification, and audit trails.
decision: Adopt Apache Kafka (AWS MSK) as the central event stream for async inter-service communication.
action: Adopted Apache Kafka for Event Bus
outcome: Enabled seamless event distribution. Rebalance storms occurred during rolling deploys before static group membership was configured.
lesson: Always enable Kafka static membership and configure proper consumer heartbeat timeouts to avoid cascading rebalances during rolling deployments.
summary: Decision to adopt Apache Kafka. Outcome: Enabled seamless event distribution. Rebalance storms occurred during rolling deploys before static group membership was configured.. Lesson: Always enable Kafka static membership and configure proper consumer heartbeat timeouts to avoid cascading rebalances during rolling deployments.

title: Architecture Decision: Adoption of Kubernetes (EKS) for Container Orchestration
author: Alex Rivera (Infra Lead), Marcus Brody (Lead DB Admin)
event: Architecture proposal for Kubernetes (EKS) in Core Infrastructure

outcome: Achieved sub-minute node scaling and simplified preview environments.
lesson: Proper resource requests/limits (CPU and Memory) and Horizontal Pod Autoscaler policies are non-negotiable to avoid node-level OOM cascading panics.

title: Architecture Decision: Replacing Redis with Multi-Tier Local LRU & DynamoDB in Recommendation Service
author: Priya Sharma (Backend Lead), Elena Vance (Principal Architect)
event: Architecture proposal for Local LRU + DynamoDB in Recommendation Service
context: Redis incident INC-101 demonstrated that network roundtrips to shared Redis cluster under bursty recommendation traffic created hot shards and thundering herds.
decision: Deprecate Redis for the Recommendation Service in favor of a 2-tier architecture: In-process Local LRU (Go-cache) backed by AWS DynamoDB with single-digit ms point reads.
action: Adopted Local LRU + DynamoDB for Recommendation Service
outcome: p99 latency dropped from 145ms to 8ms. Recommendation availability rose from 99.85% to 99.99%.
lesson: For read-heavy localized scoring models, in-memory local caches with deterministic invalidation outperform remote shared Redis clusters.
summary: Decision to adopt Local LRU + DynamoDB. Outcome: p99 latency dropped from 145ms to 8ms. Recommendation availability rose from 99.85% to 99.99%.. Lesson: For read-heavy localized scoring models, in-memory local caches with deterministic invalidation outperform remote shared Redis clusters.

title: Architecture Decision: Database Connection Pooling with PgBouncer
author: Marcus Brody (Lead DB Admin), Elena Vance (Principal Architect)
event: Architecture proposal for PgBouncer in Core Platform
context: Resolve incident INC-102 where microservice pod autoscaling spawned 1,200 direct DB connections, crashing PostgreSQL backend processes.

lesson: Transaction pooling disables prepared statements across sessions unless `server_reset_query` or binary protocol extensions are properly configured.
summary: Decision to adopt PgBouncer. Outcome: PostgreSQL CPU utilization dropped from 85% to 22% during peak sales traffic.. Lesson: Transaction pooling disables prepared statements across sessions unless `server_reset_query` or binary protocol extensions are properly configured.

title: Architecture Decision: Tenant Isolation and Sharding Strategy

outcome: Passed external SOC2 Type II audit with zero findings. Query planner overhead remained under 3%.
lesson: Always index composite keys `(tenant_id, id)` and bypass RLS only via securely gated background maintenance workers.

title: Architecture Decision: Unified Caching Strategy v2: Tiered Cache Invalidation & Eviction Safeguards

context: Synthesize lessons learned from INC-101, ADR-002, and ADR-006 into a rigorous architectural standard.

lesson: Caching is not a one-size-fits-all tool. Workload characterization (read/write ratio, access distribution, acceptable staleness) must precede caching technology selection.

title: Incident: Redis Cache Stampede Causing Recommendation Service Outage
author: Priya Sharma (Backend Lead)
event: Outage/Degradation in Recommendation Service & Redis Cluster (P1 - Critical)
context: p99 latency surged from 18ms to 4,800ms; Recommendation Service error rate hit 85%; Primary PostgreSQL CPU pinned at 100%.
decision: Emergency remediation led by Priya Sharma (Backend Lead)
action: Scaled up PostgreSQL Aurora read replicas.; Applied an emergency hotfix adding mutex locking (single-flight) on cache miss.; Introduced ±20% randomized jitter to cache TTLs.; Decided in postmortem to initiate architectural review of Redis caching strategy (led to ADR-006).
outcome: Cache stampede mitigated by single-flight query coalescing and TTL jitter. Service stabilized at 14:22 UTC. (Impact: $45,000 estimated lost conversion revenue; 120 customer support tickets.)
lesson: Never use fixed TTLs on high-traffic keys. Implement single-flight / mutex query coalescing on cache misses to prevent thundering herd database destruction.
summary: Incident in Recommendation Service & Redis Cluster. Root Cause: A marketing flash push notification sent 50,000 concurrent users to the homepage. The Redis cache key for default recommendation rankings expired simultaneously (zero TTL jitter). 50,000 requests simultaneously bypassed the cache and hit the un-indexed complex SQL join query on PostgreSQL, saturating all DB worker threads.. Lesson: Never use fixed TTLs on high-traffic keys. Implement single-flight / mutex query coalescing on cache misses to prevent thundering herd database destruction.

The Redis cache key for default recommendation rankings expired simultaneously (zero TTL jitter). 50,000 requests simultaneously bypassed the cache and hit the un-indexed complex SQL join query on PostgreSQL, saturating all DB worker threads.

title: Incident: Database Connection Exhaustion During Black Friday Traffic Burst
author: Marcus Brody (Lead DB Admin)
event: Outage/Degradation in Core PostgreSQL & Microservices (P1 - Critical)
context: All backend services logged `FATAL: remaining connection slots are reserved for non-replication superuser connections`; HTTP 500 errors across 90% of endpoints.
decision: Emergency remediation led by Marcus Brody (Lead DB Admin)
action: Temporarily reduced pod replica count and lowered local connection pool sizes.; Restarted PostgreSQL to clear stale idle connections.; Authored and approved ADR-010 to deploy PgBouncer connection pooling.
outcome: Immediate pod throttling restored database access; PgBouncer was deployed within 10 days. (Impact: 42 minutes of complete payment and checkout unavailability.)
lesson: Application-level connection pooling does not scale under elastic Kubernetes autoscaling. Centralized connection poolers like PgBouncer are mandatory.
summary: Incident in Core PostgreSQL & Microservices. Root Cause: Kubernetes Horizontal Pod Autoscaler scaled 6 microservices from 4 pods to 30 pods each. Each pod had a local connection pool size of 20, attempting to open 3,600 simultaneous persistent TCP connections to PostgreSQL, which had a `max_connections` limit of 1,000.. Lesson: Application-level connection pooling does not scale under elastic Kubernetes autoscaling. Centralized connection poolers like PgBouncer are mandatory.

title: Incident: Kafka Consumer Group Cascading Rebalance Storm

event: Outage/Degradation in Kafka Event Bus & Billing Consumers (P2 - Major)
context: Billing event processing lag climbed to 450,000 messages; CPU usage on worker pods spiked to 100% with continuous rebalancing logs.

summary: Incident in Kafka Event Bus & Billing Consumers. Root Cause: A rolling deployment triggered rapid pod terminations. Long GC pauses and default 3000ms heartbeat timeouts caused the Kafka broker to repeatedly mark alive consumers dead, triggering a continuous feedback rebalance loop.. Lesson: In Kubernetes environments with frequent pod cycling, static group membership is essential to prevent rebalance cascades.

title: Incident: Split-Brain Condition During PostgreSQL Primary Failover
author: Marcus Brody (Lead DB Admin)
event: Outage/Degradation in Aurora PostgreSQL Primary Cluster (P1 - Critical)
context: Conflicting transaction IDs logged; some writes succeeded on old primary while new writes routed to promoted replica.
decision: Emergency remediation led by Marcus Brody (Lead DB Admin)
action: Isolated the old primary node and demoted it to read-only.; Executed automated reconciliation script to merge 48 divergent records from WAL logs.; Lowered Route53 / internal DNS TTLs to 5 seconds and enabled aggressive fencing.
outcome: Data reconciliation verified 100% consistent; DNS TTL lowered. (Impact: 48 invoice records required manual reconciliation; customer transactions were paused for 40 minutes.)
lesson: Failover automation must strictly enforce STONITH (Shoot The Other Node In The Head) fencing before replica promotion.
summary: Incident in Aurora PostgreSQL Primary Cluster. Root Cause: An AWS AZ network partition triggered an automatic replica promotion, but network fencing did not sever connectivity to the isolated old primary fast enough while DNS TTLs were set to 300s.. Lesson: Failover automation must strictly enforce STONITH (Shoot The Other Node In The Head) fencing before replica promotion.

title: Incident: CloudFront Stale Cache Serving Deprecated JavaScript Bundles
author: Zack Taylor (Frontend Lead)
event: Outage/Degradation in CloudFront CDN & Frontend SPA (P3 - Moderate)
context: Users reported broken UI buttons and JavaScript runtime exceptions: `Uncaught TypeError: window.__nova_auth is undefined`.
decision: Emergency remediation led by Zack Taylor (Frontend Lead)
action: Created CloudFront cache invalidation for `/*`.; Updated S3 deployment script to set `Cache-Control: no-cache, no-store, must-revalidate` specifically for `index.html` while keeping immutable 1-year cache on hashed JS/CSS assets.; Documented in ADR-011.
outcome: CDN cache invalidated; deployment pipeline updated. (Impact: Frontend UI glitch affected approximately 450 active users.)
lesson: HTML entrypoints must never be cached with long TTLs; only content-hashed static assets should have immutable cache headers.
summary: Incident in CloudFront CDN & Frontend SPA. Root Cause: CI/CD deployment script pushed new `index.html` referencing new chunk hashes, but CloudFront CDN cache TTL for `index.html` was configured with `Cache-Control: public, max-age=86400` without automated invalidation.. Lesson: HTML entrypoints must never be cached with long TTLs; only content-hashed static assets should have immutable cache headers.

metadata.root_cause: CI/CD deployment script pushed new `index.html` referencing new chunk hashes, but CloudFront CDN cache TTL for `index.html` was configured with `Cache-Control: public, max-age=86400` without automated invalidation.

title: Incident: HashiCorp Vault Token Expiry Causing Microservice Auth Blackout
author: Sarah Jenkins (Security Lead)
event: Outage/Degradation in Vault Secrets & Service Mesh (P1 - Critical)
context: All 14 backend microservices began logging `403 Permission Denied: token expired` when attempting to fetch database credentials; all API calls failed.
decision: Emergency remediation led by Sarah Jenkins (Security Lead)
action: Issued emergency root token to kickstart service accounts.; Updated Vault agent configuration with exponential retry loops and fallback grace periods.; Added Prometheus alert for Vault token TTL < 4 hours.
outcome: Tokens refreshed and automated renewal watchdog deployed. (Impact: 32 minutes of global API downtime.)
lesson: Authentication agents must have resilient retry loops and proactive alerts for impending token expiration.
summary: Incident in Vault Secrets & Service Mesh. Root Cause: The Vault agent sidecar token renewal loop encountered a transient HTTP 500 error from Vault during a minor cluster maintenance. The renewal script did not retry and silently exited, causing tokens to expire 24 hours later.. Lesson: Authentication agents must have resilient retry loops and proactive alerts for impending token expiration.

metadata.root_cause: The Vault agent sidecar token renewal loop encountered a transient HTTP 500 error from Vault during a minor cluster maintenance. The renewal script did not retry and silently exited, causing tokens to expire 24 hours later.

title: Incident: DynamoDB Hot Partition Key Throttling in Search Indexer
author: Dave Chen (Senior Engineer)
event: Outage/Degradation in DynamoDB & Search Index Pipeline (P2 - Major)
context: Search index lag increased by 3 hours; `ProvisionedThroughputExceededException` errors flooded Datadog.
decision: Emergency remediation led by Dave Chen (Senior Engineer)
action: Enabled DynamoDB On-Demand capacity mode temporarily.; Redesigned partition key schema to use synthetic sharding: `created_date#hash(tenant_id, 8)`.; Re-indexed search table.
outcome: Synthetic sharding distributed write throughput evenly across 32 partitions. (Impact: Search results delayed by 2 hours for newly uploaded items.)
lesson: Never use monotonically increasing values or date strings as raw partition keys in NoSQL distributed databases without synthetic salt sharding.
summary: Incident in DynamoDB & Search Index Pipeline. Root Cause: The partition key was chosen as `created_date` (YYYY-MM-DD). All writes for the current day targeted a single physical storage partition, exceeding the 1,000 WCU per-partition limit despite high overall table capacity.. Lesson: Never use monotonically increasing values or date strings as raw partition keys in NoSQL distributed databases without synthetic salt sharding.

metadata.root_cause: The partition key was chosen as `created_date` (YYYY-MM-DD). All writes for the current day targeted a single physical storage partition, exceeding the 1,000 WCU per-partition limit despite high overall table capacity.

title: Incident: S3 Ingress Network Saturation During Nightly Financial ETL
author: Alex Rivera (Infra Lead)
event: Outage/Degradation in Asset Pipeline & Financial ETL (P3 - Moderate)
context: Web application PDF report downloads timed out during 02:00 UTC nightly backup window.
decision: Emergency remediation led by Alex Rivera (Infra Lead)
action: Restructured S3 key hierarchy to prefix with hash suffixes (`s3://novastack-data/{hash(id)}/...`).; Applied rate limiter to ETL download worker pool.
outcome: S3 prefix partitioning resolved rate limits; PDF download latency returned to normal. (Impact: No data loss; background ETL took 45 minutes longer to complete.)
lesson: Organize high-throughput S3 storage keys with randomized or hashed prefix namespaces to maximize AWS S3 partition distribution.
summary: Incident in Asset Pipeline & Financial ETL. Root Cause: The financial reporting ETL batch worker opened 500 concurrent multipart download threads from the same S3 prefix without request rate smoothing, hitting S3 prefix rate limits (3,500 PUT / 5,500 GET per prefix/sec).. Lesson: Organize high-throughput S3 storage keys with randomized or hashed prefix namespaces to maximize AWS S3 partition distribution.

metadata.root_cause: The financial reporting ETL batch worker opened 500 concurrent multipart download threads from the same S3 prefix without request rate smoothing, hitting S3 prefix rate limits (3,500 PUT / 5,500 GET per prefix/sec).

title: Incident: Unhandled gRPC Deadline Exceeded Causing Worker Thread Exhaustion
project: Payment Gateway to Risk Evaluation Service
technology: Payment Gateway to Risk Evaluation Service
author: Priya Sharma (Backend Lead)
event: Outage/Degradation in Payment Gateway to Risk Evaluation Service (P2 - Major)
context: Payment gateway HTTP threads hung indefinitely; client requests timed out after 60s with 504 Gateway Timeout.
decision: Emergency remediation led by Priya Sharma (Backend Lead)
action: Set default 2000ms deadline on all outbound gRPC stubs.; Configured circuit breaker pattern with resilience fallback to review queue.; Updated team gRPC boilerplate standards in ADR-008.
outcome: Deadlines deployed; unblocked threads and restored payment throughput. (Impact: 110 payment attempts timed out and required retry.)
lesson: Every RPC call without a strict deadline is an outage waiting to happen. Never instantiate a gRPC client stub without context timeouts.
summary: Incident in Payment Gateway to Risk Evaluation Service. Root Cause: The gRPC client connecting the Payment Gateway to the Risk Service did not specify a `grpc.deadline`. When the Risk Service stalled on a third-party credit check API, all Payment Gateway worker threads blocked waiting indefinitely.. Lesson: Every RPC call without a strict deadline is an outage waiting to happen. Never instantiate a gRPC client stub without context timeouts.
tags: payment gateway to risk evaluation service

metadata.root_cause: The gRPC client connecting the Payment Gateway to the Risk Service did not specify a `grpc.deadline`. When the Risk Service stalled on a third-party credit check API, all Payment Gateway worker threads blocked waiting indefinitely.

title: Incident: JWT Secret Key Rotation Misconfiguration During Deployment
author: Sarah Jenkins (Security Lead)
event: Outage/Degradation in Auth Service & API Gateway (P2 - Major)
context: All active logged-in users suddenly logged out and received `401 Unauthorized: invalid signature`.
decision: Emergency remediation led by Sarah Jenkins (Security Lead)
action: Re-published previous public JWKS verification key alongside the new key in JWKS endpoint.; Updated key rotation policy to retain previous keys for 48 hours.; Documented dual-key verification requirement.
outcome: Dual JWKS key set restored session validity for existing users. (Impact: Approximately 3,800 active users were forced to re-authenticate.)
lesson: Cryptographic key rotation must always support N-1 key overlap verification until all active token lifetimes have elapsed.
summary: Incident in Auth Service & API Gateway. Root Cause: The automated secret rotation pipeline deleted the previous public verification key (JWKS) immediately upon publishing the new key, rather than supporting a dual-key grace overlap period for currently active 1-hour access tokens.. Lesson: Cryptographic key rotation must always support N-1 key overlap verification until all active token lifetimes have elapsed.

metadata.root_cause: The automated secret rotation pipeline deleted the previous public verification key (JWKS) immediately upon publishing the new key, rather than supporting a dual-key grace overlap period for currently active 1-hour access tokens.

title: Incident: Background PDF Generator Worker Thread Starvation
author: Dave Chen (Senior Engineer)
event: Outage/Degradation in Document Generation Service (P3 - Moderate)
context: End-of-month financial PDF statements queued for 4 hours; document download latency exceeded SLA.
decision: Emergency remediation led by Dave Chen (Senior Engineer)
action: Isolated Chromium rendering into dedicated detached worker containers with CPU resource limits.; Migrated document generation queue to Kafka DLQ pipeline (ADR-019).; Added horizontal autoscaling based on queue length.
outcome: Isolated worker cluster cleared 15,000 PDF backlogs within 30 minutes. (Impact: Monthly invoice delivery delayed by 3 hours for Pro tier customers.)
lesson: Heavy CPU-bound tasks (like browser rendering or cryptography) must never execute directly in the async I/O event loop.
summary: Incident in Document Generation Service. Root Cause: Headless Chromium PDF rendering processes were launched synchronously inside the main async event loop worker process, blocking CPU cores and starving async I/O socket events.. Lesson: Heavy CPU-bound tasks (like browser rendering or cryptography) must never execute directly in the async I/O event loop.

metadata.root_cause: Headless Chromium PDF rendering processes were launched synchronously inside the main async event loop worker process, blocking CPU cores and starving async I/O socket events.

title: feat(cache): Replace shared Redis with DynamoDB & in-process LRU
author: Engineering Team
event: cache stampede vulnerability
context: Shared Redis cluster had 15ms p99 network latency and suffered cache stampedes when 50,000 keys expired concurrently during flash sales.
decision: Implemented single-flight request coalescing mutexes on cache misses, added +/- 20% randomized TTL jitter to eliminate synchronized key expirations, and deployed AWS DynamoDB with on-demand capacity as the authoritative secondary store.
action: Deployed AWS DynamoDB with on-demand capacity as the authoritative secondary store, implemented single-flight request coalescing mutexes on cache misses, and added +/- 20% randomized TTL jitter to eliminate synchronized key expirations.
outcome: Recommendation score read latency dropped from 18ms to 3.2ms p99, Redis cluster infrastructure costs reduced by $4,200/month, and zero cache stampede errors during subsequent marketing surges.
lesson: All caching layers must enforce randomized TTL jitter (+/-20%) and single-flight request coalescing. Shared in-memory caches must not be used for high-throughput read-heavy services.
summary: Mitigated cache stampede vulnerability identified in INC-101 by replacing shared Redis cluster with local in-process Go-cache LRU backed by AWS DynamoDB for immutable long-term scores.
